sentences.text:
..... For the State .
 In Re: IA NO: CRAN 2 of 2023  1.
Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has submitted that initially charged was framed in this case under Section 498A/306/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

But subsequently appellant/accused convicted under Section 498A/306 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced him to suffer simple imprisonment for a term of two (02) years and also to pay fine of Rs.3000/-, in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for another one (01) month for the offence punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

He was also sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a term of seven (07) years and also to pay fine of Rs.6000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for another two (02) months for the offence punishable under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has referred to the observation of learned Judge regarding offence under Section 304B alleged in this case, according to him, which could not be proved by the prosecution.
3. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the State has raised objection by referring to the judgment.
4. From the record, it appears that during trial the appellant was on bail.
5. Considering the observation of the learned Judge as well as term imprisonment, the prayer for bail stand allowed.

In case of change of address appellant shall inform the same to the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station mentioned above, and also the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Suri, Birbhum.
In case of violation of the order passed hereinabove, learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Suri, Birbhum will be at liberty to cancel the bail bond.
7. Accordingly CRAN 2 of 2023 stands disposed of.
